text: Four agents out, each on its own port with its own scratch dir, and only one of them allowed to edit the runtime file so they cannot lose each other work. opus5-1 is building the tracker labelling you asked for, 2/3/4 are reproducing the three bugs you just filed. I am holding the settings-scroll fix: a wheel inside any scrollable overlay now stays in that overlay instead of zooming the board. Writing its regression test next.

Settings scroll is fixed and in Review. Cause was not the panel: the viewport wheel handler called preventDefault on everything that reached it, and the toolbar lives inside the viewport, so a panel with overflow auto could never scroll. Now the first scrollable thing on the way up gets the wheel, which fixes every overlay at once instead of naming them one by one. Notes are exempt so markdown wheel routing is untouched, 6 cases plus fullscreen still green.

All three diagnoses applied and tested. Alt-drag copy is one undo now (the clone creates and the drag move fold into one batch). Previews resize both ways and stop painting outside their box. Pinch no longer dies when a finger lands on a note. Every fix has a test I proved can fail without it. The adversarial pass paid for itself twice: it caught that removing the preview clamp would have made app nodes 2.6x worse, and that the pinch patch missed the text-node-being-edited case, which is the state a phone is usually in. The mobile CRASH itself is going back to To do: no crash was ever reproduced, and the fix found underneath it is speed-independent so it does not explain your report.

Back on the board. Preview server is up again on 4174 (it was down). Reading the Review column and the open To do lane before pulling anything: nothing is claimed right now, and no new verdicts have landed since your Firefox-alt issue, which is already fixed and in Review.

Pulled both p1 PDF cards, they are the same area. Good news from the read: the fix for the pointer one already exists in the codebase, it is just wired to YouTube only. The transparent shield that keeps wheel-zoom and middle-drag pan working over a video, and hands the pointer to the content on first click, is generic in its logic and gated behind one isYouTube check. Ungating it covers PDFs and every embedded website at once. Building that plus the fullscreen button now.

Both p1 PDF cards are done and in Review. The pointer fix turned out to be a one-line gate: the shield that kept wheel-zoom and pan working over YouTube was general in its logic and wired to isYouTube only, so PDFs, embedded sites and app nodes all get it now. Fullscreen uses the browser native API rather than a copy of the markdown overlay, because re-parenting an iframe reloads it and would lose a PDF page position. 8 new cases, proved they fail without the fix, and verified against a real PDF node on the cosmoboard in a headed browser. Nothing on disk was touched: autosave off and saves blocked in every probe.

Two bug cards corrected while I was in there. The cosmoboard layout test is NOT red, it passes, and the camera the card blamed is not in the file: it passes by luck of where the camera was left. The real fault is that panning a board autosaves its camera, so a board with no defaultViewport opens wherever the last session stood. Cosmoboard and braindump are the two without one. That needs one decision from you, it is on the card. Also read the grid for the mobile crash: it is 240000px square, purely decorative, and no JavaScript touches it at all, so capping it to the viewport cannot break anything.

Your two decisions are on the board. Viewport: leaving it alone, card parked to Backlog with the mechanism recorded so it is not re-raised as a bug. Mobile crash: no blind fix, card stays To do blocked on your phone, and the full USB debugging setup is written on it so that session takes minutes. Nothing else claimed. Preview server is on 4174.

Fanned out four agents on the rest of the To do lane, each on its own port and its own test file, none of them allowed to touch braindump.js or braindump.css: 5 on shift-constrained drag, 6 on toolbar auto-hide plus page lock (coupled, since the lock icon has to survive the collapsed state), 7 on light mode and the custom theme group, 8 on pin-to-viewport. They prove patches in the running page and hand them back; I stay the single writer of the runtime so nobody loses anyone else work. I am taking the two YouTube cards myself since I already have that code open.

Both YouTube cards are in Review. The header shows the real video address on every live embed now, and a double-click selects and copies it. Videos remember where you left off, written to the node so it survives a reload rather than dying with the iframe. Two bugs of my own that the tests caught: the pause path returned early when the value had not changed and so never saved, and keying the save off onStateChange missed pauses because the player reports them through infoDelivery too. Verified end to end against the real player: played to 8s, node remembered 8, after reload the embed asked for start=8. 8 hermetic cases plus the live round-trip; stage gate and both YouTube suites green.

One trade you should judge on the address card: making the text sweep-selectable would have cost the drag handle, since for a live embed the header is the only place left to grab (the shield owns the iframe). Measured at a 7px gap on a 480px node. I kept dragging and made the double-click do the selecting. Easy to flip if you would rather have the sweep.

Shift-constrained drag is applied and in Review. Agent 5 returned a clean anchor-based patch, seven hunks, and I applied it to the runtime: 9/9 on its own suite against the real file, and the pen tool shift-snap it could have collided with is still 12/12. The design detail worth keeping: the axis anchors on the drag origin, not on where you pressed Shift, so a late press snaps to a clean line rather than inheriting the wobble. No tolerance window either, unlike the pen tool, because you asked for movement restricted to those axes rather than nudged toward them.

Caught your new card about not being able to zoom over a markdown note, and you were right: it was a regression from last session settings-panel scroll fix. That fix routes a wheel to the first scrollable thing on the way up, and it checked for a board node inside the walk rather than before it, so any note long enough to overflow matched on its own body first. The board stopped zooming over exactly the notes worth reading. Fixed, and pinned with a test that asserts the real camera moves, which is the hole the old suite had: it only checked the event reached the viewport, which it always did.

Widened the regression net around the drag change: esc-deselect 5/5, node size and overflow, resize handle clipping, mobile pinch zoom 5/5, save-reload e2e, all green. Light mode came back from agent 7 with a re-derivable sweep script rather than 242 hand-written hunks, which is the right shape: I dry-ran it against the live files and all four JS anchors still match. Holding it to apply LAST, because agent 6 is adding settings UI in exactly the region its hunks anchor on, and the sweep re-derives from whatever the files are at apply time.

Pin-to-viewport is applied and in Review, 12/12. Two changes you should overrule if you disagree: Ctrl+Tab is impossible (measured with a real OS keystroke, the browser eats it before the page sees it, and preventDefault cannot stop a tab switch) so it is Ctrl+click now; and the Windows-style snapping is filed as a follow-up rather than shipped half-built. The core is solid: the item is never re-parented out of the board layer, it just gets the inverse of the camera, so a live embed keeps the same iframe and the same JS context across pin, pan, zoom and unpin. Stored geometry is untouchable by construction, the pin box lives in a Map and never on the node.

Also: sorry about the tracker error you hit. Adding a card failed with Section Test failures is not in todo.md because my bulk edits had flipped the whole file to Windows line endings, and the server finds a lane by matching a newline before the heading. Converted back, all five lanes resolve again, 115 cards intact. Noted so it does not recur.

All four agent features are applied and green. Order mattered: the theme sweep went last and re-derived itself, so it swept the toolbar/lock CSS too (250 colour occurrences, up from 242). Three of its four JS anchors had drifted onto the settings region the lock patch rewrote, so I re-anchored them by folding the lock lines into both halves of each hunk rather than dropping either feature.

Three real problems the verification found, all fixed. A perf-budget run that got killed mid-flight had left 114 storm nodes in the sandbox board, which was breaking markdown-wheel-zoom and vnc-node; restored from the seed and both pass. The pin patch broke board-shift-snap-runtime, not by changing behaviour but because that test scrapes source for the FIRST viewport mousedown handler and the pin chord registers one above it; it now picks the handler by what it contains. And cosmoboard-initial-layout was red from your live tab autosaving its camera, which you decided to leave alone, so the TEST now pins a fixed camera and exercises the layout code instead of the drift.

Performance holds after all of it: idle 16.8ms p95, drag 83.4, pan 99.9, zoom 166.6 (budget 220, software raster), and pointer dispatch 4.85us against a 25us budget, so the pin hook and the shift-drag recompute cost nothing measurable. Also fixed a flaky assertion in the new theme suite: it read a toolbar colour mid-transition, so 1 run in 3 saw the resting grey instead of the accent. Transitions are disabled for that suite now, 4 runs clean.

Done. The To do lane is empty except the mobile crash, which is waiting on your phone. Whole suite green: board, build, features, export, preview. Site rebuilt, server on 4174, nothing committed. Five new cards are in the backlog from re-reading the roadmap, with my priority calls and the reasoning on each so you can overrule them: a CLI over the same board data (p2, the migration plan names canvas/markdown/CLI as three views over one store and two of three exist), touch parity for the new gestures (p2, pin needs Ctrl and shift-drag needs Shift, so neither exists on a phone), a shortcuts reference (p2, everything added this session is invisible), a terminal node (p3), and an audit for tests that assert mechanisms instead of outcomes (p3, which is how the markdown zoom regression got in).
